problem_summary.summary: Return a deep copy of the connected undirected graph reachable from the supplied node, preserving values and neighbor links.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a Node reference or null. Return the corresponding cloned Node reference, with cloned neighbor lists.
constraints: The graph is connected when the input node is non-null

brute_force.explanation: Use recursive DFS with a map from each original node to its clone. Create and register a clone before visiting neighbors, which also handles cycles and back-edges.
brute_force.correctness_idea: The map ensures one clone per original node. Each original neighbor is recursively mapped to its clone and appended in the same order, so the resulting reachable graph is structurally identical and shares no original nodes.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(V + E), visiting each node and neighbor reference once.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(V) auxiliary for the clone map and recursion stack; the returned clone itself uses O(V + E) space.

optimized.explanation: Perform iterative BFS. Create the start clone and map it before enqueueing; whenever an original neighbor is first seen, create and enqueue its clone, then connect the current clone to it.
optimized.correctness_idea: BFS eventually visits every node reachable from the start. The identity map guarantees a one-to-one clone for each original node, and processing every neighbor reference reproduces all edges, including cycles.
optimized.time_complexity: O(V + E), with every reachable node enqueued once and every edge reference processed once.
optimized.space_complexity: O(V) auxiliary for the map and queue; the returned clone itself uses O(V + E) space.

steps.condition: The start node has no clone yet.
steps.action: Map original 1 to a distinct clone with value 1.

steps.event: Process original node 1 and discover node 2.
steps.action: Create clone 2 and connect clone 1 to clone 2.

steps.condition: Clone 1 already exists; clone 3 does not.
steps.action: Connect clone 2 to clone 1, create clone 3, then connect clone 2 to clone 3.
Connect clone 3 to clone 2; return clone 1.

edge_cases.handling: Both methods return null without allocating a graph.
The result is a distinct node with the same value and an empty neighbor list.
Register each clone before exploring or enqueueing neighbors; mapped nodes prevent infinite revisits.

edge_cases.case: Two originals with the same value outside the stated uniqueness rule
edge_cases.handling: Mapping uses node identity, not values; each object would still receive its own clone.
